title: Udu (clay pot drum)
summary: The udu is a clay pot drum from the Igbo people of Nigeria, first made by potters as a water jug. A large hole in the side and a small opening in the neck turn the pot into a drum: slapping the side hole gives a deep, bending bass, and the body answers with sharp strokes.
howToPlay: The pot lies on a woven mat: the big hole faces you and the neck points to the right.
The side hole gives the deep bass, the neck opening a hollow boom, the belly a short tap and the shoulder a dry click.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the steady bass and tap, then add the neck and the shoulder.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar, played in eighth notes.
heritageNote: Igbo women potters made the first udu, and the pot is still played in dance bands and in modern ensembles around the world. Its two openings let the player bend the pitch by opening and closing the hand over each one.
